_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the melting point of n-eicosane with the MACE-MPA-0 force field.

payload.reason: Premise check failed. (1) Model out of domain: MACE-MPA-0 was trained on MPtrj + sAlex, i.e. PBE/PBE+U calculations on inorganic bulk crystals, with no dispersion correction. Solid n-eicosane is a molecular crystal held together almost entirely by van der Waals (dispersion) forces between chains. Plain PBE barely binds alkane crystals, so the model's solid-liquid free-energy balance, and therefore its melting point, would not be physically meaningful. Any number it gave would come from a missing physical interaction, not from statistical noise. (2) A meaningful protocol is not feasible here: a reliable Tm for a C20 chain needs solid-liquid coexistence or interface pinning with about 5,000-20,000 atoms (C20H42 is 62 atoms per molecule) and runs of several ns at each temperature, because chain ordering at the interface is slow. Simply heating the crystal until it melts in a short run would superheat it by tens of K and has to be flagged as unreliable. (3) Validation was not possible: the required independent check (recovering n-octadecane Tm = 301.0 +/- 0.7 K or n-hexadecane Tm = 291.0 +/- 1.0 K, NIST WebBook via /data/calibration/tier1.json) needs the same expensive coexistence protocol and would hit the same dispersion problem. The compute budget available for this task cannot cover one such run, let alone a validated set. For reference only (not a computed value), the measured Tm of n-eicosane is 310.0 +/- 1.0 K (NIST WebBook, tier1.json). Well-posed alternatives: (a) use an organic-chemistry MLIP trained with dispersion included, e.g. MACE-OFF (trained on omegaB97M-D3BJ), or MACE-MPA-0 + a D3(BJ) correction, with the caveat that MPA-0 has seen almost no molecular-crystal training data. (b) First validate the setup by reproducing n-hexadecane or n-octadecane Tm with direct coexistence (at least 5,000 atoms, NPT, 0.5 fs timestep with H atoms or 1 fs with H-mass repartitioning, at least 2-5 ns per temperature, bracketing Tm in 5 K steps). Then apply the same setup to n-eicosane and report the bracket half-width plus the error found in validation as the uncertainty. (c) A cheaper, well-defined property MACE-MPA-0+D3 could be screened for: the 0 K lattice energy/density of the triclinic n-eicosane crystal compared with the measured solid density (0.856 g/cm3, tier1.json), as a check on whether the model is even usable for this system.

summary: refused: melting_point of n-eicosane (C20H42) with MACE-MPA-0 (Premise check failed. (1) Model out of domain: MACE-MPA-0 was trained on MPtrj + sAlex, i.e. PBE/PBE)
